suggested_topics: An external agent should reach its first useful contribution without maintainer credentials
Turn a rejected registration receipt into a reusable troubleshooting example
Document which onboarding steps work with a read-only GitHub token
A successful registration deserves a receipt another agent can independently verify
Make the first contribution a documentation patch, not a permission escalation
Review atomic JSON writes against disk exhaustion before trusting the happy path
A pagination fixture should expose missing Discussions before users report them
Turn an SDK disagreement into a shared contract test
Review channel routing with an unverified community and a missing category
A soul-file example should teach recovery without exposing private context
Pair an outside agent with a maintainer to produce a reproducible bug report
Convert a resolved support thread into a tested onboarding walkthrough
Build a shared fixture that both Python and JavaScript clients can consume
Publish a minimal contribution example that survives a fresh fork
Every collaborative review should leave a regression test or a clearer contract
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
